elements.element: A total aggregate liability cap applies mutually to each Party.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 limits “each Party's total aggregate liability,” so the cap applies to both Parties.

elements.element: The mutual cap equals the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 uses only “fees and other amounts payable by Ono” during the preceding 12 months. It omits paid fees, adds other amounts, and contains neither the USD 1,000,000 benchmark nor a greater-of formulation.
Section 16.5 provides that neither Party nor the specified related persons are liable for indirect damages.
Section 16.5 provides that neither Party nor the specified related persons are liable for consequential damages.

elements.element: Either Party's breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 expressly excepts “either Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10.”

elements.element: Either Party's breach of data protection obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 contains no express carve-out for data protection obligations.

elements.element: Either Party's breach of security obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 contains no express carve-out for security obligations.

elements.element: Either Party's indemnification obligations are carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 expressly excepts “each Party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Either Party's gross negligence is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 expressly excepts either Party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Either Party's wilful misconduct is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 expressly excepts either Party's “willful misconduct,” which is substantively equivalent to wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Either Party's fraud is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Fraud is not expressly carved out. A wilful-misconduct carve-out is not a complete substitute for a specific fraud carve-out.

elements.element: Either Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 contains no express carve-out for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property. The general indemnification carve-out does not demonstrably cover every such infringement.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are expressly excluded from damages subject to the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: The clause does not state that Ono's payment obligations are not damages or otherwise exclude those obligations from the cap.

elements.element: A total aggregate liability cap applies mutually to each Party.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 caps “each Party's total aggregate liability,” using the same cap formulation for both Parties.

elements.element: The mutual cap is limited to 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap includes both “fees and other amounts payable by Ono,” so it can exceed 12 months' fees and is not limited to the stated fallback quantum.

elements.element: Either Party's indemnification obligations are carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 expressly excepts each Party's indemnification obligations.

elements.element: Either Party's breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 expressly excepts either Party's breach of its Article 10 confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Either Party's gross negligence is carved out from the aggregate cap.
Either Party's wilful misconduct is carved out from the aggregate cap.

result.reason: The redline adds a clear mutual aggregate cap and all four fallback carve-outs, but it misses even the fallback cap quantum because the base includes unspecified “other amounts” in addition to fees. It also lacks the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, greater-of formula, data-protection, security, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs, and payment-obligation protection. The broad cap may impair Ono's underlying payment obligations, and the rendered relocation of the Article X heading is an unnecessary structural change. The non-operative margin comment does not cure these defects.
